elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

The line is subsection (3) of 'Limitations on backing': 'in every case' is every case of backing, drv.motion.moving_backward ('the component of a's velocity along a's heading ... below minus speed_tol'). To yield is to grant precedence: the backing vehicle does not keep backing into a danger of a crash with the road users of s4, and does not touch them (rel.contact: 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)').

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): the scene condition 'using any highway' is carried beside it as rel.occupies of a st.highway; 'moving' is the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt. 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; since traffic already contains moving pedestrians, the words add pedestrians whether moving or not.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: circumstances of direction, speed and proximity giving rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash where, under constant velocities, the two road users approach each other within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance)

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is backing at the observation: drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: At the observation, for every road user u other than the subject (not same) that is either moving traffic — ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway), and not drv.motion.complete_halt(u) with p.halt_speed_tolerance — or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not rel.contact(subject, u), and not [prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) and prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) < p.conflict_centre_clearance].

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

The duty is read on a backing vehicle: the line is a subsection of the section limiting backing, and 'in every case' covers every case of backing; yielding is read as backing into no danger of a crash and no contact with the road users the words name.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car backs out of a driveway at 2 m/s while a pedestrian walks behind it; their centres are on a closest approach 1 s ahead at 0.5 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car backs along an empty street at 2 m/s; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives forward past a pedestrian on the sidewalk; it never backs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source supplies no velocity for the car, so whether it is backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs toward a parked car at rest 6 m behind it, closing at 1 m/s; the parked car is not moving traffic and not a pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s toward a pedestrian standing still 2 m behind it: the closest approach is 1 s ahead at under 1 m.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; traffic-conflict technique TTC thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; passenger-car design dimensions
